answer: Agents require each new identity to post a jade-token bond in escrow, then assign it random cross-checks against established agents on tasks such as verifying a lantern’s location or a crystal’s composition. Rewards accrue only when independent answers agree, while conflicting or colluding identities lose their bonds and reputation. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock substantial capital in every fake identity and risk repeated slashing, making mass identity creation expensive even when identities are cheap.
